subject: Hosted API commit step-up & tier rebalance proposal
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit step-up & tier rebalance proposal

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the sync last week. EdgeCommerce's traffic patterns from March show sustained growth in chat & embeddings volume (thank you for the dataset you shared). Based on the consumption curve and the burst behavior, we recommend a staged commit increase that preserves per-token economics while giving you predictable capacity through Q4.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Current hosted monthly commit: 3M tokens/month
- Proposed baseline commit: 6M tokens/month (effective June 1)
- Burst pocket: additional 2M tokens/month for 30% higher short-term spikes (soft burst window)
- New rate tier: moving from Tier B -> Tier A pricing for baseline usage (lower unit price)
- Soft throttle policy: automatic soft-throttling at 110% sustained over 10 minutes, with a 2-week grace period during initial 60-day ramp

Why this helps EdgeCommerce:
- Lowers per-token cost on the baseline usage you care about (chat sessions)
- Predictable throughput for peak shopping hours with a small burst cushion
- Can be rolled out with a 2-week pilot that preserves existing SLA during the test

I've attached a draft SOW and a March usage export that backs these numbers. Marissa is copied for ops/throughput verification. If this looks reasonable, we'll put together a DocuSign-ready SOW and a proposed start date (target June 1) and route through procurement.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick confirmation on whether procurement prefers a June 1 effective date or a July 1 start.
2) Procurement review of the attached SOW (I can move to a minimal redline with pricing locked).
3) Two-week pilot window in May to validate burst behavior and KV-cache tuning.

Happy to hop on a 30min call tomorrow if you want to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan | Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Tessa —

Appreciate the detailed breakdown and the export. A few quick clarifications from our side before procurement will sign off: 

1) Can you confirm the per-token unit price at the proposed baseline (6M)? The SOW PDF is useful but procurement needs line-item pricing in a spreadsheet.
2) What's the exact billing cadence — monthly in arrears vs. monthly prepaid? We prefer aligned billing with our fiscal months (month-end).
3) For the soft throttle and burst pocket: if we exceed the burst pocket, what does the overage path look like (rate, immediate throttle vs queued requests)?
4) Legal will want a clause for data residency (we need logs retained for 90 days and audit export capability).

Looping in procurement and Dan from infra who will verify whether the two-week pilot works for our production traffic windows. If June 1 is tight, we can consider July 1, but we'd like the pricing sheet to evaluate the cashflow impact.

Thanks — happy to take a call mid-day Monday.

—Samantha
Samantha Lee | Head of ML Products, EdgeCommerce

>

> 2) What's the exact billing cadence — monthly in arrears vs. monthly prepaid? We prefer aligned billing with our fiscal months (month-end).
> 3) For the soft throttle and burst pocket: if we exceed the burst pocket, what does the overage path look like (rate, immediate throttle vs queued requests)?
> 4) Legal will want a clause for data residency (we need logs retained for 90 days and audit export capability).

Thanks for the callout — answers inline below and attached a pricing sheet that breaks out the line items. Also attached a slightly revised SOW that includes a 90-day log retention addendum.

Answers (summary):
- Pricing (baseline 6M): $0.0009 per token for baseline volume (Tier A). Burst pocket overage rate: $0.0018 per token (50% premium above baseline).
- Billing cadence: Monthly in arrears, invoices issued at month close. We can provide an optional monthly prepaid lane; happy to discuss which fits EdgeCommerce cashflow.
- Overage behavior: once the burst pocket is exhausted in a billing cycle, requests will be soft-throttled (response with HTTP 429) for sustained bursts; customers may opt into immediate overage billing to avoid 429s (we can auto-unlock for a pre-agreed payment method). Our ops team will also provide a monitoring dashboard and 24/7 escalation for the first 30 days of the ramp.
- Data residency & logs: SOW v3 now includes 90-day log retention and an exportable audit bundle (S3 or secure Drive share). For additional residency constraints (e.g., EU-only storage), we can open a Private deployment conversation.

Attachments in this message: commit_pricing_sheet.xlsx (line items), EdgeCommerce_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW with retention addendum), usage_reports_Mar2026.csv

Proposed near-term plan:
1) Procurement reviews pricing sheet — aim for procurement sign-off within 5 business days.
2) Two-week pilot during May 10-24 to validate throttle behavior and KV cache tuning (team: Marissa to run ops).
3) If pilot passes, effective date: June 1; DocuSign link to follow for SOW signature.

If procurement prefers a July 1 start, we can shift the pilot into late May/early June and lock pricing to the proposal above.

Would you like a 20min walkthrough of the pricing sheet Monday? I'm available 11am or 3pm PT.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan | Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
